I kind of went over all of my thoughts on the season overall in the last rewatch thread. In terms of comments related specifically to the 2nd half of the first season I really don’t have that much to say. Yui gets introduced (and removed) in this half of the season, and I really like Yui. Those 2(?) episodes with her are some of the most adorable things I’ve ever seen. She is kind of used as a cop out with the admin stuff, but the situation that she gets mc and company out off only arises because of Yui, so it’s not that big of a deal imo. The admin terminal is also only used to save “Yui’s Heart”, so I don’t really have an issue with Yui’s god powers. They don’t show up again in ALO that much IIRC. I really like the Parent-child relationship, I just wish that , much like everything in the Aincrad arc, that it was extended and explained more in depth. This is a classic gripe with SAO though, not much you can do.

When I was watching it the first time, I didn’t expect Heathcliff to be Kayaba. That was a pretty cool twist on my first watchthrough. I wonder why he did the immortal object, HP never falls to the yellow zone. The only thing that I can think of is that he wanted it as a status symbol, as an “HOLY SHIT Heathcliff’s HP never goes into the yellow! Dude!” type thing. As the game creator, he surely could have made it so his HP never goes to 0, but reaches the last sliver of red that shows up a couple of times. He most likely could have disabled his nervegear’s (does he even use one?) death trap, or a myriad of other options besides never going to yellow. However never going to yellow fits the character's personality I think, so whatever.

Pros

  • Kirito Asuna Relationship. So good, so satisfying.

  • Yui. See above.

  • More boss fights. There are two? boss fights in this half I think? The final one is awesome, and the one before that with the army was pretty cool as well.

  • The lakehouse episodes. I loved these. Gave a really cool insight into the world of the game and how people were living out their “lives” as it were.

Cons

  • Plot armor. I don’t have an issue with Asuna rushing through the cliffs to save Kirito, that's believable. Why was Kirito able to grab the sword and try to pull it out? I get it was showing his fear of death and need for Asuna, but come on just show him thinking that, not grabbing the sword. Why was Asuna able to jump in front of Heathcliff’s sword? Why was Kirito able to kill Heathcliff after he’d been killed? (It seems like Kayaba wanted this to happen, but that's a lame excuse anyway.)

  • Guilds. I wanna see more of the major guilds. We got some insight into the army, which was dope. I wanted to see more of Laughing Coffin. We kind of, kind of get this in SAO II but even then it’s not much. We saw some of the Knights of the Blood Oath, which was cool. Do they get their own floor? It seemed like it. Do all major guilds have this? So many questions.

  • Pacing. Draw out stuff more, everyone and their mom has been over this issue.

Overall still really good. 7.5/10 arc IMO. The season overall is good even with Fairy Dance Arc. Took me a few tries to get past the Fairy Dance villain smelling Asuna’s hair and sticking his finger in her mouth and shit, but I still like and appreciate that arc damnit! SAO isn’t a disease!

It could be difficult to talk about this set of 8 episodes without basically restating all of the criticisms I made of this arc from the first 6 episodes, but whatever. Apologies for any later arc spoilers that I unintentionally left unspoilt. Link to my thoughts on the first 6 episodes

Episode 7 carries on Kirito's adventures through Aincrad, and there really isn't much to be said about it past what I said about episodes 3-6. To add onto this, we also got the beginning of episode 13 and parts of episode 11 building upon the world, but they didn't get that much time put onto them due to other events. I still like the worldbuilding in this arc.

The rest of the show spends time focusing on the couple of Kirito and Asuna, being transformed from two good friends to a in-game married couple. Episodes 8-10 took up the majority of this couple development, whilst episodes 11-13 focused more on Kirito and Asuna just being a couple, similar to how episodes 3-7 went. I really don't have too much wrong with Kirito and Asuna becoming a couple like this, as it felt sort of realistic. Unlike Silica and Lisbeth, who ended up falling in love in Kirito almost immediately after they met him, at least Asuna took time to fall in love with Kirito. It took two years to progress from the moment they met for them to properly fall in love.

The main problem with the romance was that there wasn't enough time spent developing the couple before episode 8. I can understand that Kirito and Asuna were good friends by episode 8, but the only development of their relationship before that was episodes 5/6. Then in episode 7, we see Asuna and Kirito were quite good together. I feel like I missed something between that. Which harks back to my complaint about this show from the first discussion thread of this show, with the show just jumping around between certain events.

Alongside the romantic build-up, we also got a continuation on the main story of beating SAO. They didn't focus on a group of people working together however, it was mostly focused on Asuna and Kirito. They did bring in Klein and his guild during the boss fight, but the actual fight didn't feel like a group of people working together as with episode 2. It was just Kirito and Asuna managing to beat the boss on their own, helped by Kirito having a special ability which he just so happens to debuts. It was weird, seeing as the very next boss battle managed to kill a number of people from the top guilds, but the boss right before that was able to be defeated mainly by just two people.

The part with Asuna's bodyguard turning out to be a murderous traitor wasn't something I found particularly good. I know that he hated Kirito, but I didn't see it as so far as to murder him. It made no sense when I watched it, and it only seemed as something there to push Kirito and Asuna together. There was very little (if any) foreshadowing in the show which would suggest he would make a move like that. He really didn't have anything to gain from murdering two people within the guild. Hell, Laughing Coffin (the murder guild the bodyguard was a part of) had only been established in the previous episodes, there wasn't any real development towards them in the show. They murdered for the sake of murder, and they just so happened to aim for Kirito because...some guy was embarrassed by him? I didn't particularly like this.

Episodes 11-12 were the Yui arc. What do I say about that? I'm not going to call 'Yui being a part of the game' an ass-pull. The game bugging out at the end of episode 11, whilst it is just skipped over like nothing happened, and Yui not having a user cursor, nor having any NPC pop-ups from being carried by them. They did hint at it, so I can't be too mad about it. I wasn't exactly a fan of them doing at right as Kirito and Asuna were about to be killed, though there wouldn't have been many other circumstances which that could be told in an entertaining manner like how it was revealed.

Now, I get onto the final boss fight and what follows from here. The actual boss fight was pretty good, and it was one of my more favourite ones from this arc, even though it was all over so quickly in the beginning of episode 14. The fight between Kirito and Heathcliff there (and the duel they had at episode 10) were also entertaining, but...the ending of this fight...sigh what an ass-pull. 'Kirito and Asuna's love and sheer willpower saved the day'. It also broke a pretty important rule where if you died, you couldn't do anything. That affected everyone who had died in that game beforehand. Why didn't Asuna come back via willpower? Why didn't Sachi say to the god of death 'Not today'? It was one of the worst scenes from SAO for me. Then there is also the reason that Akihiko made SAO and trapped thousands of people in it...wait, what was that again?

So Aincrad. As I said, it is the best arc of Sword Art Online, but that isn't saying much to be fair. Sword Art Online isn't going to be show I'll ever hold up as a masterpiece of storytelling or whatever, or something I'll hold up for strong characters, or for amazing writing and dialogue. Sword Art Online isn't a particularly notable show, especially with how saturated this type of story is becoming within anime (single dude is OP and can solve everything and has harem of girls; for example: Pick Up Girls In Dungeon, Irregular At Magic High School). The pacing isn't exactly that good, it skips over a whole bunch of stuff which could have made for good storytelling, the ending was bollocks. There is quite a fair bit which is bad or just plain mediocre with it when you analyse it.

I will give Aincrad something: It is an entertaining arc to watch, in the same sense of Kekkai Sensen, or Kill la Kill. If I go in-depth into the show, then I can see the flaws from it. However, if you were just to view it at face value, then it's an enjoyable show. That should be noted. The boss fights are done quite well, with good animation, character designs and OST mixing well together. The character interaction does have its charms at times. Kirito & Asuna's relationship was quite nice.

Yeah. Aincrad. If you know what you are getting yourself into when you start watching it, then you can have an enjoyable time. However, if you've read both my posts, you've had the arc spoiled for you now, so...sorry

May we not go off and rewatch the rest of this show.

BONUS COMMENT: Just on a additional note, I want to compare Sword Art Online to another MMO show which aired after Aincrad: Log Horizon. In terms of being a MMO anime, I'd say that Log Horizon is better than Sword Art Online. What Log Horizon does is go really in depth to explain what its MMO and how everything is, way more than SAO does. Sword Art Online's worldbuilding is pretty basic. They do have a different target audience though.

With Log Horizon, the show's worldbuilding is quite in-depth. They spend time to properly explain the MMO it's set in and what has happened to the players as they have been trapped within the MMO. It goes pretty in-depth into how the game's classes work, how the combat mechanics work, guild systems, NPCs, food, flavour text, different servers and so on and so forth. There is a lot within that show. There isn't a lot of action sequences in it though, at least in comparison to SAO. There's 2 arcs in a row in season 1 (10 episoddes) where the main characters of the show are not involved in any fighting scenes, and there are a number of lore dumps within both seasons of the show which people could find boring.

The main audience that Sword Art Online is targeting might not necessarily want that. SAO doesn't aim to be an in-depth show about what being in a MMO is like, it just aims to be an entertaining show. The fights are enjoyable to watch. The soundtrack works well with the show and everything happening with it. It is a 'popcorn' show, and it works well at being something you can just sit back and enjoy (most of the time). Having something like Log Horizon's lore dumps could just end up not working for Sword Art Online.

I personally prefer Log Horizon over Sword Art Online. I like Log Horizon spending time to properly expand the world and build up the lore within it. That's more entertaining for me. Sword Art Online does something completely different though, and that could be why I don't like it as much. For what Sword Art Online does, it does a nice job at it, but it isn't necessarily what I look for within an MMO anime.

However, it needs to be acknowledged that Sword Art Online is just more accessible. I suppose the most popular thing isn't a really in-depth world, but straight-up action. The Transformers movies must be pretty successful for a reason, and I'm not sure that is because of the writing in it, instead of robots beating the crap out of each other. SAO just ticks all of the boxes to being an enjoyable show for as many people as possible, and it should get some credit for that.
